conventions.convention: The exterior is the compact manifold S³ minus the interior of a specified closed normal-disk tube. Its orientation comes from S³; its boundary has the exterior boundary orientation. Tube, fibre norm and radius are input data.

A positive knot tangent followed by an oriented normal-plane basis gives the ambient orientation. The meridian is the oriented normal-disk boundary. A preferred longitude has degree +1 over the oriented core and zero image in integral exterior homology; uniqueness concerns its homology class.
The product section σ is an arbitrary framing section and is not asserted to be the preferred longitude.
The exterior and peripheral results assume countable choice. The normal-circle trivialization lemma instead gives a finite construction without that assumption.
The homology theorem uses product Euclidean disk coordinates and requires the tubular-map domain to contain the closed radius-2ε disk bundle.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice and the stated smooth oriented knot, oriented normal trivialization and product tubular map whose domain contains S¹ × D²₂ε. Then H₁(E_K; Z) ≅ Z is generated by [μ]. The kernel of H₁(T_K; Z) → H₁(E_K; Z) is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class [λ] with p_*[λ] = 1. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and ([μ], [λ]) is a basis of H₁(T_K; Z).

Assume countable choice. Every smooth oriented knot admits the stated oriented trivialization and tubular map containing a radius-2ε disk bundle. Its closed radius-ε tube is a solid torus; its exterior is a compact smooth oriented three-manifold with torus boundary. The open complement strongly deformation retracts onto the exterior.

Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood, the positive fibre meridian μ and product section σ form a basis of H₁(T_K; Z). The section is not asserted to be the preferred zero-homology longitude.
For every smooth oriented embedding K:S¹ → S³, the quotient normal bundle, oriented by the tangent-then-normal convention, admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism ν_K ≅ K × R².

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 invokes [F6], thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude, for the displayed tube with ε = 1/√2. That theorem requires its tubular-map domain to contain the radius-2ε disk bundle. The displayed map Φ(t,w) = (exp(2πit)√(1−|w|²),w) is defined only for |w| < 1, whereas 2ε = √2. Thus the citation's explicit radius hypothesis is not discharged for these data. The explicit solid-torus coordinates already give a short direct homology verification, so the mathematical conclusion remains readily supported.

alerts.finding: In [F4], lem-zero-filling-of-fibered-knot-is-a-torus-bundle attributes to thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude: “the preferred longitude is the unique primitive boundary class that maps to zero”. Both [λ] and −[λ] are primitive kernel classes. The supplier states uniqueness with the additional normalization p_*[λ] = 1. Proof 2.1 correctly uses the unoriented conclusion “up to orientation”, so the defect is the wording of the cited fact.

The Definition begins “Work in the smooth category ([[def-smooth-manifold]])” and contains numerous further inline wikilinks throughout the complete definition. This published prerequisite violates the uninterrupted-definition requirement; the links have not been moved to an immediately following Definition references section.

The Definition says “Equip S with the smooth structure supplied by [[lem-slice-chart-restrictions-form-a-smooth-atlas]]” and includes another inline supplier link before completing the normal and conormal constructions. These hyperlinks interrupt the Definition rather than appearing afterward in Definition references.

The Definition includes “its normal bundle ν(S) ([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]])” and the inline link [[prop-normal-and-conormal-bundles-are-smooth-vector-bundles]] before specifying the tubular-neighbourhood data. These links violate the uninterrupted-definition requirement.

The Definition contains “for the cellular groups of [[def-oriented-cellular-chain-group]], with differentials defined in [[def-cellular-boundary-from-three-consecutive-skeleta]]” and a further inline chain-complex supplier link. The complete Definition is interrupted by hyperlinks and has no following Definition references section.

The Definition specifies its connecting map as being “from [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]], followed by the quotient map”. The hyperlink occurs inside the defining sentence rather than after the complete Definition.
